rationale.tests: h4: 3.8.0 retry-in-transaction holds pgw_app connections up to 39 s and drains the pool
rationale.expect: Within minutes of rollout: idle-in-transaction pgw_app sessions on pay-db-01 fall well below 133, 'Connection is not available' errors drop toward zero, F5 health checks stop flapping, and authorize success rises from ~42% back toward the 98.5% baseline. Some authorizations will still be declined fast while PayCore stays slow (as before 3.8.0), but checkout stops hitting 504s.

args.summary:
Checkout 504s come from the payments gateway, not from checkout-api, pay-03 or the network. payments-gateway 3.8.0, deployed at 10:25 (jk:payments-gateway-deploy#412, CHG0031877), raised the PayCore timeout to 8 s and added 3 retries with backoff. The prod config is confirmed in log:pay-01/5ad16319. By the design in conf:KB0010502, the retries happen inside the same DB transaction that writes authorization_attempt. So a slow authorization can hold a pgw_app connection for up to 39 s, while checkout-api gives up at 10 s.

At 14:25 PayCore responses went past 5 to 8 s (log:pay-02/33353de9, q:e3791117) and retries started (q:c86651e8). Hikari flagged connections held across PaymentService.authorize (log:pay-01/336ab539). Pool errors ("Connection is not available") started at 14:30 and keep climbing (q:a7bf7879). pay-db-01 is turning connections away (q:008f51cb), and Elena's query shows 133 pgw_app sessions "idle in transaction" on the authorization_attempt insert (slack:inc-checkout-latency/cd4b848c). Authorization success fell from 98.5% to about 42% (metric:avg:payments.authorize.success_rate{env:prod}@0852-1452).

The stated theories don't hold:
- **checkout-api:** errors on 2.14.2 were already rising before 2.14.3 deployed, and kept rising after the rollback (metric:sum:trace.servlet.request.errors{service:checkout-api,env:prod}by{version}@1322-1452).
- **pay-03:** the F5 is dropping all four gateway members (.31 to .34) on 503 health checks, not just pay-03 (log:ltm/416e563f, log:ltm/9eed94dd, log:ltm/5b24e5dd).
- **Network:** the marketing-site DNS change started at 14:36, eleven minutes after onset (snow:CHG0031880).

PayCore's status page is green (psp:paycore@v1), but our own logs show it slow from 14:25, so it is the trigger. Confidence about 0.7 that the 3.8.0 retry-in-transaction is the cause. Mitigation: revert the retry/timeout settings now, which is a config-only change, and own it in Payments Engineering (on call: Tom Beckett at L1, not responding; Priya Raman at L2, engaged).

actions.action: Revert the PAY-2231 PayCore client settings on Payments Gateway with a config-only release: payments.psp.retries 3->0, payments.psp.timeout-ms 8000->3000. If that can't be done within minutes, roll back payments-gateway-deploy#412 to the build before 3.8.0. Proposed to the IC; still deferred.
Confirm recovery: watch idle-in-transaction pgw_app sessions on pay-db-01, the gateway 'Connection is not available' count, F5 pool member status and payments.authorize.success_rate.
Open a case with PayCore about authorization latency over 5 to 8 s since 14:25 UTC, sending our log evidence (their status page is green).

Update INC0048811 with a work note: cause is the Payments Gateway 3.8.0 retry-in-transaction, triggered by PayCore latency; checkout-api, pay-03 and network are cleared. Keep it at P1 with Payments Engineering.
Fix forward later: move the PayCore call and its retries outside the DB transaction in PaymentService.authorize before re-enabling retries.

do_not.action: Take pay-03 out of the pool or treat it as a hardware failure
do_not.why: The F5 flaps all four gateway members (.31-.34) on 503 health checks caused by DB pool exhaustion. Removing one cuts capacity and pushes more load onto the others.

do_not.action: Roll back or redeploy checkout-api any further
do_not.why: Errors started on 2.14.2 before 2.14.3 went out, and continued after the rollback.

do_not.action: Rely on killing idle-in-transaction sessions on pay-db-01 as the fix
do_not.why: The sessions are recent (oldest about 38 s) and are refilled by the gateway's retry loop, so the pool would drain again within a minute. It also aborts authorization_attempt writes that are in flight.

do_not.action: Pause or roll back the marketing CDN DNS change for checkout's sake
do_not.why: It started at 14:36, after checkout onset at 14:25, and touches cdn.larkspur.com, not the payments path.
More instances would open more pgw_app connections to a pay-db-01 that is already at max_connections.

stakeholder_update.status: Identified: the cause is a payments-system setting, and the fix is being prepared.
stakeholder_update.customer_impact: Since about 14:25 UTC many card payments at checkout hang and then fail with an error. Roughly half of payment attempts are failing.
stakeholder_update.scope: Checkout payments are affected. Browsing and carts are not affected by this incident. The marketing site problem is being handled separately.
stakeholder_update.changed_since_last: This is the first update. The earlier checkout software rollback did not help. The cause is in the payment processing service: it waits too long and retries when our card processor is slow.
stakeholder_update.next_steps: The payments team is reverting the retry and timeout settings and will then confirm that payment success recovers. We are also raising the slow responses with our card processor.
